title: From Ingestion to Agents: How AI Teams Build on Document Intelligence — Adit Abraham, Reducto
talk_summary: Reducto's CEO describes lessons from processing billions of documents: decompose parsing into cheap CV layout detection plus VLM semantic correction, format data for its consumer (markdown vs HTML vs natural-language-for-embedding), and use agent harnesses with verification loops to fix silent recall failures. The most transferable ideas are agentic verification/correction layers, classify-and-split to shrink context, and per-stage evals.

takeaways.technique: Agentic verification/correction layer over a cheap first pass
takeaways.what_they_do: Run a cheap deterministic first pass (CV layout detection), then a VLM verification-correction layer that only makes token-level edits rather than regenerating, producing high-confidence output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have a verification correction layer that ends up leading to a high confidence output

takeaways.technique: Parent agent sets validation criteria for sub-agents
takeaways.what_they_do: For large structured extraction, a parent agent defines validation criteria that sub-agents follow, catching silent drops (missing rows/fields) that single-shot frontier models miss.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You can have a parent agent go through set validation criteria for sub agents to follow
takeaways.numbers: Frontier models with max reasoning are precise but 'silently drop a lot of the contents'; harness closed both precision and recall gap.

takeaways.what_they_do: Classify documents and route to the right pipeline/snippets rather than passing everything; quality erodes when too much context is passed, beyond token economics.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there is erosion that you find in quality outside of just the token economics as a result of passing in too much

takeaways.what_they_do: Eval each pipeline stage (parsing, retrieval, formatting, final agent performance) plus real-time production monitoring, since production data differs from contrived sets.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the best teams that we work with look at eval on a granular level for each step of their pipeline

takeaways.technique: Format data for its consumer (markdown vs HTML vs NL-for-embedding)
takeaways.what_they_do: Use markdown for simple tables, HTML only for complex merged-cell tables, and a separate natural-language representation for embedding/retrieval, because embedding models struggle with tag-heavy HTML.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're using the HTML table representation. And when you're trying to make sure that you retrieve the right snippets, you're using that natural language block

takeaways.technique: Right tool per task: small CPU models for structure, big models for semantics
takeaways.what_they_do: Use sub-million-parameter CV models (CPU-runnable) for layout/structure detection and reserve VLMs for semantic correction, hitting an accuracy/cost/latency frontier.
takeaways.evidence_quote: subund million parameter models are really effective for things like detecting the layout of a document
